ai_analyses.response:
VULN: Microsoft SMB (SMBv1) | SEVERITY: CRITICAL | PORT: 445 | SERVICE: microsoft-ds  
DESC: Windows 8.1 Pro 9600 SMB service exposes vulnerabilities like EternalBlue (CVE-2017-0144) and lack of SMBv1 patches.  
FIX: Disable SMBv1, enable SMBv3, and apply all Microsoft security updates for Windows 8.1.  

VULN: Microsoft RPC (DCOM) | SEVERITY: HIGH | PORT: 135 | SERVICE: msrpc  
DESC: Unauthenticated RPC endpoints may allow remote code execution via vulnerabilities like CVE-2017-0144.  
FIX: Restrict RPC access to trusted IPs, disable unused DCOM services, and patch Windows.  

VULN: NetBIOS (SMB) | SEVERITY: HIGH | PORT: 139 | SERVICE: netbios-ssn  
DESC: NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NBT) can be exploited for session enumeration and SMB relay attacks.  
FIX: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP and restrict SMB traffic to internal networks.  

VULN: Microsoft HTTPAPI (UPnP) | SEVERITY: MEDIUM | PORT: 2869 | SERVICE: http  
DESC: Exposes UPnP/SSDP services which may allow unauthorized device discovery or configuration changes.  
FIX: Disable UPnP if not required and restrict access to internal networks.  

VULN: Open SMTP (Relay) | SEVERITY: HIGH | PORT: 25 | SERVICE: smtp  
DESC: Unauthenticated SMTP service may allow email relay attacks if not properly configured.  
FIX: Implement SMTP authentication, disable relay, and use TLS for email traffic.  

RISK_LEVEL: CRITICAL  
SUMMARY: The target runs unpatched Windows 8.1 with multiple vulnerable services (SMB, RPC, SMTP) exposed. SMBv1 and outdated OS pose critical risks for exploitation. Immediate patching and network segmentation are required.
